category: PCB query language: object-type, layer and field keywords
description: Keywords of the PCB query language used in rule scopes, the PCB Filter/List panels, Find Similar Objects and output filters: object-type checks (Is...), layer checks (On...), field keywords and operators. All keywords are case-insensitive; string arguments use single quotes and support * and ? wildcards where noted.

tools.name: IsPad (query function)
tools.description: Returns all pad objects, both free pads and component pads, on any layer. Combine with attribute checks such as IsSMTPin/IsThruPin, HoleSize, or layer checks to narrow the set. The most common building block of clearance and mask rule scopes.
tools.example: IsPad And OnMultiLayer And (HoleSize >= 1mm)   -- through-hole pads with 1 mm or larger drills
tools.notes: IsComponentPad restricts to pads owned by components; IsFree And IsPad gives free pads.

tools.name: IsVia (query function)
tools.description: Returns all via objects. Refine by span with IsThruVia, IsBlindVia, IsBuriedVia, IsMicroVia, IsSkipVia, IsStackedVia, by drill pair with InDrillLayerPair('Top Layer - Bottom Layer'), or by role with IsStitchingVia / IsShieldingVia / IsTeardrop.
tools.example:
IsVia And InNet('GND') And Not IsStitchingVia
IsVia And (HoleSize < 0.25mm)   -- microvia candidates
tools.notes: Via templates are matched with IsLinkedToPadViaTemplate('name').

tools.name: IsTrack (query function)
tools.description: Returns straight track segments on any layer (copper, silkscreen, mechanical, keepout). Use with OnSignal/OnCopper for routing, with IsWire for routed copper (tracks and arcs on signal layers), or with IsComponentTrack for footprint outline lines.
tools.example: IsTrack And OnLayer('Top Overlay') And (Width < 0.15mm)   -- silkscreen lines too thin to print
tools.notes: Orientation helpers: IsHorizontal, IsVertical, IsOblique, IsObliquePositive, IsObliqueNegative; length: TraceLength, ManHat.

tools.name: IsArc (query function)
tools.description: Returns arc objects (including full circles). Arc geometry can be tested with the field keywords ArcRadius, ArcStartAngle and ArcStopAngle; IsComponentArc limits to arcs inside footprints.
tools.example: IsArc And OnCopper And (Width < 0.1mm)
tools.notes: Rounded corners created while routing are arcs and are included in IsWire.

tools.name: IsFill (query function)
tools.description: Returns rectangular fill objects. Fills are legacy solid rectangles (no cut-outs); modern designs prefer regions and polygon pours, so this query is handy for locating and converting old fills.
tools.example: IsFill And OnCopper And Not InAnyNet   -- copper fills with no net assigned
tools.notes: IsComponentFill selects fills owned by footprints.

tools.name: IsRegion (query function)
tools.description: Returns all region objects: copper regions (IsCopperRegion), polygon cutouts (IsCutoutRegion), board cutouts (IsBoardCutoutRegion), cavity regions, and keepout regions. Regions are also the primitives that polygon pours consist of after pouring.
tools.example:
IsRegion And IsCopperRegion And Not InPolygon   -- hand-placed solid copper regions
IsRegion And IsBoardCutoutRegion
tools.notes: Use InPolygon / InNamedPolygon to include or exclude pour-generated regions.

tools.name: IsPolygon / IsPoly (query function)
tools.description: Returns polygon pour objects themselves (the parent pour, not its child regions/tracks). IsPoly is an alias. To get the poured copper primitives use InPolygon or InNamedPolygon('name'); to pick one pour use IsNamedPolygon('name').
tools.example:
IsPolygon And InNet('GND') And OnLayer('Bottom Layer')
IsPolygon And AutoAssignedName = 'True'
tools.notes: Polygon pour cutouts are regions (IsCutoutRegion), not polygons.

tools.name: IsText (query function)
tools.description: Returns all text/string objects including designators and comments. Sub-types: IsDesignator, IsComment, IsComponentText (any string owned by a component), IsStrokeText, IsTrueTypeText, IsBarCodeText, IsQrCodeText.
tools.example:
IsText And IsDesignator And OnSilkscreen   -- all silkscreen designators
IsText And IsTrueTypeText And OnCopper
tools.notes: Text properties queried with field keywords such as Text, StringType, Height (see the Fields reference).

tools.name: IsComponent (query function)
tools.description: Returns component (footprint instance) objects, not their child primitives. Combine with membership checks (InComponentClass, WithinRoom), package checks (IsBGA, IsSMTComponent) or field keywords (Comment, ComponentType, Rotation) to build placement rule scopes and List-panel views.
tools.example:
IsComponent And OnBottom And IsThruComponent
IsComponent And (Comment Like '10k*')
tools.notes: InAnyComponent returns components plus their children; IsComponentPrimitive returns only children.

tools.name: IsComponentPad (query function)
tools.description: Returns pads that belong to placed components (excludes free pads). Typical in clearance rules between component pads and other copper, and in paste/solder mask rules that must not affect free test pads.
tools.example: IsComponentPad And InComponentClass('BGA') And IsSMTPin
tools.notes: Related child-object checks: IsComponentTrack, IsComponentArc, IsComponentFill, IsComponentVia, IsComponentBody, IsComponentText.

tools.name: IsKeepOut (query function)
tools.description: Returns keepout objects of every primitive kind (arc, fill, region, track) that have the Keepout attribute set, whether on the Keep-Out Layer or restricted to a specific copper layer. Use it to review or bulk-edit keepouts, e.g. to restrict which object kinds they block.
tools.example:
IsKeepOut And OnLayer('Top Layer')
IsKeepOut And IsRegion
tools.notes: Keepouts on the global Keep-Out Layer match OnLayer('Keep-Out Layer').

tools.name: IsDimension (query function)
tools.description: Returns every dimension object; sub-types match the Place > Dimension menu: IsLinearDimension, IsAngularDimension, IsRadialDimension, IsLeaderDimension, IsDatumDimension, IsBaselineDimension, IsCenterDimension, IsLinearDiameterDimension, IsRadialDiameterDimension, IsOriginalDimension (the legacy Standard dimension).
tools.example: IsDimension And OnMechanical And (DimensionTextUnit = 'Millimeters')
tools.notes: Dimension formatting fields (DimensionTextHeight, DimensionArrowSize, DimensionTextPrecision...) are listed in the Fields reference.

tools.name: IsCoordinate (query function)
tools.description: Returns coordinate marker objects (Place > Coordinate), which display the X/Y position of a point. Useful to find and delete stale coordinates on mechanical layers before output.
tools.example: IsCoordinate And OnMechanical
tools.notes: Formatting fields share the CoordinateDimension* keywords.

tools.name: IsConnection (query function)
tools.description: Returns ratsnest connection lines (unrouted connections), which lets the PCB Filter highlight or count remaining connections for a net or class.
tools.example: IsConnection And InNetClass('DDR')   -- unrouted DDR connections
tools.notes: Connections are not selectable design primitives; use them for filtering/masking only.

tools.name: IsNet (query function)
tools.description: Returns net objects (the net entities themselves), enabling net-level tests such as NetLength, NetPinCount, NetViaCount, Color and IsElectrical in the PCB List panel or Filter.
tools.example:
IsNet And (NetPinCount = 1)   -- single-pin nets
IsNet And (NetViaCount > 4)
tools.notes: For objects belonging to a net use InNet / InNetClass instead.

tools.name: IsClass (query function)
tools.description: Returns class objects (net, component, layer, pad, from-to, differential pair, polygon, structure, xSignal, design channel classes). ClassType field distinguishes them; used mainly in the PCB List panel to audit classes.
tools.example: IsClass And (ClassType = 'Net Class')
tools.notes: Objects in a class are queried with the In...Class membership keywords.

tools.name: IsRule / IsRule_<Kind> (query function)
tools.description: IsRule returns all design rule objects; the IsRule_<Kind> family selects one rule type, e.g. IsRule_Clearance, IsRule_MaxMinWidth (Width), IsRule_RoutingViaStyle, IsRule_ShortCircuit, IsRule_BrokenNets (Un-Routed Net), IsRule_MinimumAnnularRing, IsRule_MatchedLengths, IsRule_ConfinementConstraint (Room Definition), IsRule_MaxMinHeightConstraint (Height), IsRule_TestPointStyle, IsRule_ReturnPath. Rules then appear in the PCB List panel for bulk editing of names, scopes and enabled state.
tools.example: IsRule_Clearance   -- in the PCB List panel: edit Gap and scopes of all clearance rules at once
tools.notes: Names follow the internal rule kind, not the UI label (Width = MaxMinWidth, Hole Size = MaxMinHoleSize, Length = MaxMinLength, Impedance = MaxMinImpedance).

tools.name: IsDifferentialPair (query function)
tools.description: Returns differential pair objects (the pair definitions). For the routing primitives of a pair use InDifferentialPair('name') or InAnyDifferentialPair; for pairs in a class use InDifferentialPairClass.
tools.example: IsDifferentialPair And (Name Like 'USB*')
tools.notes: Pairs are created in the PCB panel's Differential Pairs Editor mode or from schematic directives.

tools.name: IsRoom (query function)
tools.description: Returns room objects (Room Definition rules as placed on the board). Use WithinRoom('name') / TouchesRoom('name') to get the objects inside a room.
tools.example: IsRoom And OnLayer('Bottom Layer')
tools.notes: IsRule_ConfinementConstraint is the rule-object equivalent.

tools.name: IsTeardrop (query function)
tools.description: Returns the region objects that teardrops are built from (Tools > Teardrops), allowing them to be selected, hidden in a filter or excluded from clearance scopes.
tools.example:
IsTeardrop And OnLayer('Top Layer')
IsRegion And Not IsTeardrop
tools.notes: Removing teardrops should be done through Tools > Teardrops > Remove rather than deleting the regions.

tools.name: IsStitchingVia / IsShieldingVia / InViaShielding (query functions)
tools.description: IsStitchingVia returns vias placed by Tools > Via Stitching; IsShieldingVia returns vias placed by Tools > Via Shielding; InViaShielding returns vias and polygons that are members of a shielding group. These let rules (e.g. Hole To Hole, Clearance) treat automatically placed vias differently from routed ones.
tools.example: IsVia And Not IsStitchingVia And Not IsShieldingVia   -- vias placed by routing
tools.notes: Stitching/shielding groups are edited from their Properties panel entries.

tools.name: IsThruVia / IsBlindVia / IsBuriedVia / IsMicroVia / IsSkipVia / IsStackedVia (query functions)
tools.description: Via span checks matching the Via Types defined in the Layer Stack Manager: through vias, blind vias (start on an outer layer), buried vias (both ends internal), microvias (uVia flag), skip vias (uVias spanning more than one dielectric) and stacked vias. Use them to give HDI vias their own Routing Via Style, annular ring and hole-size rules.
tools.usage: IsThruVia | IsBlindVia | IsBuriedVia | IsMicroVia | IsSkipVia | IsStackedVia
tools.example:
IsMicroVia And Not IsStackedVia   -- single-level microvias
HasViaType('Type III')             -- IPC-4761 classification
tools.notes: HasViaType and HasViaFeature (Capping, Covering, Filling, Plugging, Tenting) query the IPC-4761 protection settings; InDrillLayerPair selects by drill pair name.

tools.name: IsSplitPlane (query function)
tools.description: Returns split plane objects on internal plane layers (the regions created by split lines). Use in the Filter to inspect plane assignments or in a rule scope for Power Plane Clearance.
tools.example: IsSplitPlane And InNet('VCC_1V2')
tools.notes: Split planes are managed in the PCB panel's Split Plane Editor mode.

tools.name: IsEmbeddedBoard (query function)
tools.description: Returns embedded board array objects (Place > Embedded Board Array) used for panelisation. Field keywords EmbeddedBoard_DocumentName, EmbeddedBoard_RowCount, EmbeddedBoard_ColCount, EmbeddedBoard_RowSpacing and EmbeddedBoard_ColumnSpacing expose their settings.
tools.example: IsEmbeddedBoard And (EmbeddedBoard_RowCount > 1)
tools.notes: Panels reference child .PcbDoc files by path; check EmbeddedBoard_DocumentName after moving projects.

tools.name: IsViolation / HasViolations (query functions)
tools.description: IsViolation returns the DRC violation marker objects; HasViolations returns design objects whose violation state is true. Use in the PCB Filter to mask everything except violating objects, or in the List panel to export them.
tools.example: HasViolations And IsTrack   -- tracks currently in violation
tools.notes: Markers are (re)generated by online DRC or Tools > Design Rule Check; Tools > Reset Error Markers clears them.

tools.name: IsSelected / IsComponentSelected / IsNetSelected (query functions)
tools.description: IsSelected returns currently selected objects; IsComponentSelected returns the child primitives of selected components; IsNetSelected returns net-aware objects belonging to any net that has a selected object. They let a Filter or List view work on the current selection and are used by Find Similar Objects results.
tools.example: IsNetSelected And IsVia   -- vias on the nets of the selected tracks
tools.notes: In the PCB List panel switch the view to 'Filtered objects' to combine with the query.

tools.name: IsObjectKind / ObjectKind (query keywords)
tools.description: IsObjectKind('Kind') tests the object kind string; the ObjectKind field can be compared with = or Like. Kind strings include 'Arc', 'Pad', 'Via', 'Track', 'Text', 'Fill', 'Region', 'Polygon', 'Component', 'Component Body', 'Dimension', 'Coordinate', 'Net', 'Class', 'Rule', 'Room', 'Connection', 'Embedded Board', 'Differential Pair', 'xSignal'.

parameters.name: ObjectType
parameters.description: Kind string as shown in the Properties panel/List panel Object Kind column.

tools.example: ObjectKind = 'Component Body' And OnLayer('Mechanical 13')
tools.notes: The Is<Kind> keywords are usually clearer; ObjectKind is convenient in List-panel column filters.

tools.name: All (query keyword)
tools.description: Matches every object on the document. Used as the default rule scope, to clear a filter, or as one side of a binary rule (e.g. clearance between a net class and All).
tools.example: Clearance rule: first object InNetClass('HV'), second object All, 2 mm.
tools.notes: Related: IsFree (free primitives only), InAnyNet, InAnyComponent.

tools.name: OnLayer (query function)
tools.description: Returns objects on the named layer; the name is the layer's display name from the Layer Stack Manager / View Configuration panel ('Top Layer', 'Bottom Layer', 'Mid Layer 1', 'Internal Plane 1', 'Top Overlay', 'Mechanical 1', 'Keep-Out Layer', 'Multi-Layer' or a custom name such as 'GND_PLANE'). Pads on Multi-Layer are not matched by OnLayer('Top Layer'); use ExistsOnLayer for that.

parameters.name: Layer
parameters.description: Exact layer display name (string, wildcards allowed).

tools.example:
IsTrack And OnLayer('Top Layer') And InNetClass('DDR')
OnLayer('Mechanical 1') And IsDimension
tools.notes: Renaming a layer breaks rule scopes that use its name; ExistsOnLayer('Top Layer') also matches multilayer pads/vias that have copper there.

tools.name: ExistsOnLayer (query function)
tools.description: Returns objects that physically exist on the named layer, including multilayer pads and vias that span it, whereas OnLayer only matches objects whose Layer property is that layer. Use it for mask/plane checks and for selecting everything a Gerber layer will contain.
tools.example:
ExistsOnLayer('Top Solder') And IsPad
ExistsOnLayer('Mid Layer 2') And IsVia   -- vias whose span includes Mid Layer 2
tools.notes: HasMaskExpansionOnLayer('Top Solder') finds objects with per-layer mask overrides.

tools.name: OnSignal / OnCopper / OnMultiLayer (query keywords)
tools.description: Layer-set shortcuts: OnSignal matches objects on any signal layer plus Multi-Layer; OnCopper matches signal layers, Multi-Layer and internal planes; OnMultiLayer matches objects whose layer is Multi-Layer (through-hole pads, vias). Faster and rename-proof compared with listing layer names.
tools.example:
IsTrack And OnSignal And (Width < 0.1mm)
IsPad And OnMultiLayer And Not IsPadHoleValid
tools.notes: OnMid restricts to internal signal layers; OnOutside to Top Layer and Bottom Layer; OnPlane to internal planes.

tools.name: OnTop / OnTopLayer / OnBottom / OnBottomLayer (query keywords)
tools.description: OnTopLayer and OnBottomLayer match only the Top Layer and Bottom Layer copper. OnTop and OnBottom match the whole side: copper plus overlay, paste and solder layers, so they return everything belonging to top-side or bottom-side components and documentation.
tools.example:
IsComponent And OnBottom          -- bottom-side components
IsTrack And OnBottomLayer And InNet('GND')
tools.notes: For component side use OnTop/OnBottom; a component's Layer property is Top Layer or Bottom Layer.

tools.name: OnSilkscreen / OnTopSilkscreen / OnBottomSilkscreen (query keywords)
tools.description: Match objects on Top Overlay and/or Bottom Overlay (the silkscreen layers). Commonly used to bulk-edit designator text size or line widths, and in Silk To Solder Mask / Silk To Silk rule scopes.
tools.example: IsText And OnSilkscreen And IsDesignator   -- then set Height/Width in the PCB List panel
tools.notes: OnMechanical matches all enabled mechanical layers; OnInverted matches negative layers (paste, solder, planes).

tools.name: OnSolderMask / OnPaste / OnTopSolderMask / OnBottomPaste (query keywords)
tools.description: Mask-layer checks: OnSolderMask and OnPaste match objects on either side's solder or paste layer plus the pads/vias that produce openings there; the OnTop.../OnBottom... variants restrict to one side. Handy for auditing manual mask objects (e.g. custom paste regions) that will appear in Gerber mask layers.
tools.usage: OnSolderMask | OnTopSolderMask | OnBottomSolderMask | OnPaste | OnTopPaste | OnBottomPaste
tools.example: OnTopPaste And IsRegion   -- hand-drawn stencil apertures on top
tools.notes: Pad-level mask overrides are found with HasMask / HasSolderMask / HasPasteMask.

tools.name: Layer (query field)
tools.description: Field keyword holding an object's layer name; compared with = , <> or Like. Equivalent to OnLayer for exact matches but usable with wildcards to match layer name patterns (e.g. all mechanical layers named 'Assy*').
tools.example: IsTrack And (Layer Like 'Mid Layer*')
tools.notes: Component objects report Top Layer/Bottom Layer; multilayer pads report 'Multi-Layer'.

tools.name: Name (query field)
tools.description: Field keyword giving the object's name: net name for nets, pad designator for pads, class/rule/room/polygon name for those objects, component designator for components. Supports Like with wildcards.
tools.example:
IsNet And (Name Like 'VCC*')
IsPad And (Name = '1') And InComponentClass('Connectors')   -- pin 1 of every connector
tools.notes: For nets the membership form InNet('GND') is usually preferable because it returns the net's primitives too.

tools.name: HoleSize (query field)
tools.description: Numeric field for the drill diameter of pads and vias, compared with units (mil default; append mm to use millimetres or wrap with AsMM). Used in Hole Size and annular-ring related scopes and to find microvias or oversized holes.
tools.example:
IsVia And (HoleSize <= 0.15mm)          -- laser-drill candidates
IsPad And (HoleSize = 0) And OnMultiLayer  -- multilayer pads without a hole
tools.notes: HasRoundHole / HasSlotHole / HasSquareHole / HasRectangularHole test hole shape; DrillType tests the drilling method.

tools.name: Width (query field)
tools.description: Numeric field for the width of tracks and arcs (and the stroke width of text/dimension lines). Compare with a unit suffix or use AsMM/AsMils to force a unit. Essential for width-audit queries and for List-panel bulk edits.
tools.example: IsTrack And OnCopper And (Width < 0.1mm) And Not InAnyComponent
tools.notes: Rule-driven width is not stored on the track; the query compares the actual placed width.

tools.name: Rotation / Comment / Component / ComponentType (query fields)
tools.description: Component-oriented field keywords: Rotation (degrees), Comment (the component comment string), Component (returns child primitives whose parent designator matches) and ComponentType ('Standard', 'Mechanical', 'Graphical', 'Net Tie', 'Net Tie (In BOM)', 'Standard (No BOM)', 'Jumper'). Handy in placement scopes and BOM-exclusion filters.
tools.example: IsComponent And (Rotation <> 0) And (Rotation <> 90) And (Rotation <> 180) And (Rotation <> 270)
tools.notes: Type checks IsStandardComponent, IsMechanicalComponent, IsNetTieComponent, IsJumperComponent, IsGraphicalComponent, IsNoBOMComponent are the boolean equivalents.

tools.name: Query operators (And, Or, Not, Like, Between, comparison)
tools.description: Boolean operators And, Or, Not (also &&, ||, !) combine keywords; comparison operators =, <>, <, >, <=, >=, and Between ... And test numeric or string fields; Like performs wildcard string matching with * (any run) and ? (one character); parentheses control precedence. Numeric values may carry unit suffixes (mil, mm, in). Strings are single-quoted and case-insensitive.
tools.usage: expr And expr | expr Or expr | Not expr | field Like 'pattern' | field Between a And b
tools.example:
(IsPad Or IsVia) And InNet('GND') And Not (HoleSize Between 0.2mm And 0.4mm)
IsComponent And (Name Like 'R?') And OnTop
tools.notes: Use the Query Helper's Check Syntax button or Mask/Apply in the PCB Filter to validate expressions before pasting into a rule scope.

tools.name: Query Helper dialog
tools.description: Dialog opened from any query field (PCB Filter, rule scope Advanced/Custom Query, List panel) that lists every query keyword grouped by category (Object Type Checks, Membership Checks, Layer Checks, Attribute Checks, Fields, Functions/System Functions) with syntax and description, inserts them into the expression, and offers Check Syntax. Pressing F1 on a keyword opens its reference page.
tools.usage: PCB Filter panel > Helper; Design > Rules > scope > Query Helper...; PCB List panel > Filter > Helper

parameters.name: Check Syntax
parameters.description: Validates the expression against the document.

tools.example: Open Query Helper from a Clearance rule's Custom Query, double-click InNetClass, type the class name, click Check Syntax, then OK.
tools.notes: The Query Builder is the alternative graphical condition-list editor for simpler scopes.
